_about: Local reference for the MITRE ATT&CK technique ids MemoryGraph tags findings with. Written for offline use: nothing here is fetched from the internet. Names follow ATT&CK v15; the descriptions are short summaries in MemoryGraph's own words, not MITRE's text. Edit or extend this file freely (keep the JSON shape).

T1003.001.summary: Reading the memory of the LSASS process (or dumping it) to extract password hashes, tickets and plaintext credentials.
T1003.001.look_for: A process that is not a Windows component holding a handle to lsass.exe with memory-read access; procdump/comsvcs/rundll32 command lines; .dmp files created shortly afterwards.

T1014.summary: Rootkit behaviour: hiding processes, drivers, files or connections from the operating system's own listings.
T1014.look_for: Objects that a scan finds but a list walk does not (psscan vs pslist, modscan vs modules, psxview columns); kernel callbacks or system-call table entries that point outside any known module.

T1027.summary: Making content hard to read or detect: encoding, encryption, packing or splitting strings.
T1027.look_for: Base64/-EncodedCommand blobs, long escaped or concatenated strings, high-entropy sections in a dumped file. Decode what you can and read where it came from.

T1036.summary: Making malicious software look like something legitimate.
T1036.look_for: Names that imitate Windows processes, a second copy of a process that is normally unique, a process whose image name and file name differ.

T1036.005.summary: Using the name or location of a trusted program (svchost.exe, lsass.exe, a system folder) for something else.
T1036.005.look_for: Core Windows process names running from the wrong folder or with the wrong parent; system DLL names loaded from a user-writable folder.

T1053.005.summary: Using scheduled tasks to run code at a time, at logon or repeatedly.
T1053.005.look_for: Task actions that run from Temp/Public/Downloads, interpreters with hidden-window, bypass or download arguments, tasks created close to the time of the incident.

T1055.summary: Running code inside another process's memory: injected PE images, shellcode, manually mapped DLLs.
T1055.look_for: Private executable memory (malfind) that starts with MZ or shellcode bytes, images mapped in a process but missing from its loader lists (ldrmodules, vadinfo vs dlllist).

T1059.summary: Using a command or script interpreter (cmd, PowerShell, wscript, mshta) to run commands.
T1059.look_for: Interpreters started by unusual parents (Office, browsers, services) or running scripts from user-writable folders.

T1059.001.summary: PowerShell used to run commands, often encoded, hidden or bypassing the execution policy.
T1059.001.look_for: -EncodedCommand / -enc, -w hidden, -ep bypass, download cradles (DownloadString, IEX). Decode the command and check the parent process.

T1071.summary: Communicating with an outside server over common application protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) so the traffic blends in.
T1071.look_for: Connections to public addresses from processes that normally have none, or from processes already flagged for another reason; check ports, state and creation time.

T1105.summary: Bringing a tool or payload from outside into the system (certutil, bitsadmin, PowerShell downloads).
T1105.look_for: Command lines with URLs or -urlcache/-f http; files that appear in Temp or Downloads shortly after such a command.

T1218.summary: Proxying execution through signed Windows binaries (mshta, rundll32, regsvr32, msiexec...) so a trusted program runs the payload.
T1218.look_for: Those binaries with a remote URL, a script (.sct/.hta) or a DLL from a user-writable folder in their arguments.

T1543.003.summary: Creating or changing a Windows service so code starts at boot, usually as SYSTEM.
T1543.003.look_for: Service ImagePath / ServiceDll outside Windows and Program Files, services running cmd or PowerShell, services missing from svcscan but present in the registry (or the reverse).

T1546.010.summary: AppInit_DLLs makes Windows load a chosen DLL into every program that uses user32.dll.
T1546.010.look_for: A non-empty AppInit_DLLs value with LoadAppInit_DLLs = 1; check the DLL's folder and whether it appears in many processes' module lists.

T1546.012.summary: Image File Execution Options 'Debugger' makes Windows start another program whenever a chosen program is launched.
T1546.012.look_for: Debugger values under IFEO (sticky-keys style hijacks of accessibility tools, Task Manager replacements). Process Explorer as taskmgr.exe replacement is a known legitimate use.

T1547.001.summary: Run/RunOnce registry keys (and the Startup folder) start a program at every logon.
T1547.001.look_for: Values pointing into Temp/Public/Downloads, encoded commands, script hosts or LOLBins; check the key's last-write time.

T1547.004.summary: Winlogon's Shell and Userinit values decide what starts at logon; adding a program to them runs it for every user.
T1547.004.look_for: A Shell other than explorer.exe or a Userinit with more than C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,

T1547.014.summary: Active Setup components run their StubPath once per user at logon, which is rarely reviewed.
T1547.014.look_for: StubPath values that run from user-writable folders or through script hosts; most legitimate entries use rundll32/regsvr32 with files in System32.

T1574.summary: Making Windows run attacker code instead of (or before) the intended code by abusing how programs find and load files.
T1574.look_for: Modules loaded from Temp/Downloads/Public or from AppData into a process that does not live there.

T1574.001.summary: DLL search-order hijacking: a malicious DLL with a legitimate name is found first by a program that loads it.
T1574.001.look_for: System DLL names (kernel32.dll, version.dll, ...) loaded from the program's own folder or another non-system folder.

T1055.012.summary: Process hollowing: a legitimate program is started suspended, its image is replaced with other code and it is resumed, so the malicious code runs under a trusted name.
T1055.012.look_for: A process whose in-memory image differs from the file on disk (headers, size, entry point), an image base that is private memory instead of a mapped file, a process started suspended by an unusual parent.

T1055.013.summary: Process doppelgänging / ghosting: code is run from a file that was modified or deleted while it was being mapped, so there is no matching file on disk to scan.
T1055.013.look_for: A running process whose image file is deleted or has no name, or a section created from a transacted or delete-pending file.

T1562.006.summary: Indicator blocking: logging or telemetry is switched off or patched so that the activity is not recorded (for example the ETW event-writing function patched to return at once).
T1562.006.look_for: ETW functions in ntdll with a different first instruction than the file on disk, disabled trace sessions, audit policy changes just before suspicious activity.
